title: Mass-gap functional determinant approach for mobile Fermi polarons
authors: Emilio Ramos Rodríguez, Eugen Dizer, Xin Chen, Richard Schmidt
abstract: We extend the functional determinant approach (FDA), previously restricted to static impurities, to the case of finite-mass impurities by using the mass-gap description of Fermi polarons [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 193401 (2025)]. The quadratic structure of the mass-gap model enables the exact evaluation of many-body spectra and Ramsey dynamics for mobile impurities. We show that this mass-gap FDA smoothly interpolates between the Fermi-edge singularity for infinitely heavy impurities and the emergence of quasiparticle weight for finite impurity mass. Our results demonstrate that the mass-gap FDA provides a transparent and computationally efficient framework to describe the quantum dynamics of mobile impurities.
summary: This paper develops and applies the mass-gap functional determinant approach to study Fermi polarons, which are impurities coupled to a Fermi gas. It successfully models the crossover between the static regime, characterized by the Fermi-edge singularity, and the mobile regime, where coherent quasiparticles form. The framework provides a quantitative description of how impurity motion regularizes the spectral features and dynamics.
main_problem: The paper extends the functional determinant approach (FDA) to describe the quantum dynamics of mobile impurities (Fermi polarons) coupled to a Fermi sea, bridging the gap between static and mobile impurity physics.
main_result: The mass-gap FDA provides a unified and computationally efficient framework that smoothly interpolates between the Fermi-edge singularity (static limit) and the formation of coherent quasiparticles (mobile limit).
method: The authors employ the functional determinant approach (FDA) applied to the quadratic mass-gap Hamiltonian derived from the Lee-Low-Pines model, utilizing Wick's theorem and mean-field approximations.
model_or_system: The system is a Fermi polaron, modeled by the Lee-Low-Pines Hamiltonian, where a mobile impurity interacts with a surrounding Fermi gas. The key theoretical tool is the mass-gap FDA, which exploits the quadratic structure of the effective Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Spectral function A(omega), Ramsey signal S(t), Quasiparticle weight Z, and the Mass Gap $\Delta(M)$.
important_parameters: Mass ratio ($M/m$), Fermi momentum ($k_F$), and the mass gap $\Delta(M) = k_F^2/M$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mass-gap Hamiltonian being quadratic, and later sections employ mean-field approximations and perturbative expansions in the interaction strength.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the single- and many-body spectra for varying mass ratios, showing Anti-Polaron (AP), Repulsive Polaron (RP), and Molecule-Hole Continuum (MHC). They also compare the time evolution of the Ramsey signal S(t) and the spectral function A(omega) across different theoretical methods.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the mass-gap FDA by analyzing the LLP Hamiltonian, derives key observables like S(t) and A(omega), and then systematically demonstrates the interpolation between the static Orthogonality Catastrophe limit and the finite-mass quasiparticle regime, comparing results against alternative methods like the Chevy ansatz.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics as it provides a rigorous theoretical tool to model impurity dynamics in ultracold atomic gases (Fermi polarons), which is a major platform for studying strongly correlated quantum many-body physics.
